correctness.rationale: Let H<=F_2^n be nontrivial. A fixed point in the geometric realization has barycentric coefficients constant on each H-orbit; its support is a union of cosets x+H, giving the orbit-simplex PL model. If any h∈H has Hamming weight >=3, every coset contains a forbidden pair and the fixed set is empty. Classifying binary subspaces with maximum nonzero weight <=2 gives rank at most two: weight-one lines, weight-two lines, coordinate two-planes, and even-weight two-planes on triples. A weight-one line gives coset graph Q_{n-1} by deletion of one coordinate; a weight-two line gives the same graph after a parity linear relabeling. Neither admissible rank-two type has compatible distinct cosets, leaving exactly 2^(n-2) discrete points. The cube has 2^(n-1) vertices and (n-1)2^(n-2) edges, giving reduced H1 rank 1+(n-3)2^(n-2). Independent coset and edge enumeration tested all admissible nonzero subgroups at n=3..6, counts 10,20,35,56, with exact graph compatibility; uniform classification comes from proof, not finite experiments.

Neither determines geometric fixed subspaces |K_n|^H: traces yield Lefschetz/Euler characteristics for single elements, not homotopy types or simultaneous fixed sets of rank-two groups. value.rationale: Geometric subgroup fixed spaces of an actual high-symmetry Rips complex are intrinsic equivariant-homotopy data, not interchangeable with homology-invariant subspaces. The theorem classifies every nontrivial translation subgroup uniformly and exhibits a sharp empty/cubical graph/discrete-set trichotomy with explicit integral homology; the rank-two phenomenon is not recoverable from an elementwise character table. This is a natural complete equivariant topology classification and useful for testing equivariant models.

limitations: Every nonzero linear binary translation subgroup H, n>=3; no claim for all isometry subgroups.
Fixed points are barycentric/geometric, not simplicial fixed vertices or homology invariants.
Finite independent test n=3..6 corroborates all-subgroup theoretical proof; no infinite experimental certification.
